surfaces.part: rusty bent sheet, concrete lumps, glass shards and cable clusters (three small debris groups)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64-px-wide rectangle on every row (0-47). It is a textured earth ground plate seen from above, with no front face, no edge line and no eave shadow. The debris (rusty sheet, concrete, glass, cable) sits on the plate as small decor clusters, and the earth patch itself has no vertical south face. This is a flat ground decal, so it reads as a top-down slab, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine. The candidate has 6 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 1%, and only 3% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown or red rather than black. The picture is weaker than the numbers. The earth is mottled in about 3-4 brown steps, below the references' 5-6 steps with per-element highlights. The debris is three or four small, nearly identical grey-and-red stamps with dark outlines. They read as stickers pasted on the soil, not as pieces shaded one by one. The sheet, concrete lumps, glass and cable are not distinguishable, and the oil stain is not visible. The whole patch, with only 34 colours, is sparser and flatter than the reference paving, so a careful artist would not accept it next to the references. Failing when in doubt.
